purpose: Defines the ceiling of what the autonomous self-healing/self-learning layer may do WITHOUT a human in the loop. Everything here is a hard boundary chosen deliberately. Anything not explicitly allowed is denied. Loaded at startup by the watch-loop and repair engine via swarm_os/services/autonomy_policy.py; the version number makes policy changes reviewable and revertable. The code enforces THIS file — it does not duplicate it.

scope_ceiling.summary: App code only. The autonomous layer may repair/modify application code, never its own orchestration/healing/security/watch/evolution machinery. The self-modify block set is directory-level AND dependency-aware: any file under the blocked dirs, plus any project file the repair machinery imports, is off-limits — even if it lives in an otherwise-allowed directory.

never_self_modify.reason: A buggy repair must not be able to damage the safety layer that is doing the repairing. Editing these paths unattended requires human sign-off. Directory-level anchors below are combined with the loader's dependency-aware scan of what the repair/watch machinery imports.

blocked_patterns_comments.scripts: scripts/ blocked: helper/ops tooling, not application logic, deliberately excluded from auto-repair scope.

hard_model_boundary.reason: Cost/trust boundary already enforced in _llm_client; kept here as the written record.

evolution.reason: Genome selection ranks by real fitness but a new generation's tool policy must be staged and reviewed before it becomes active. Nothing promotes itself.

details.staging: next generation written to data/evolution/staged/<gen>.jsonl, not active until approved
details.active_on: explicit approval (CLI command or policy approval)

rollback.reason: Automatic rollback fires ONLY on an explicit, measurable regression signal, and reverts ONLY the evidence-justified diff via the persisted snapshot/.bak — never a whole-tree revert.

concrete_conditions.post_repair_test_regression: The repository test suite (pytest) must have PASSED before the repair was accepted, AND within the canary window (default 30 min after the repair ships) a re-run of the same suite FAILS with an error attributable to the repaired file (same module in the traceback). Threshold: ANY failing test whose traceback names the repaired file or its imported module.
concrete_conditions.downstream_consumer_breakage: Within the canary window (default 30 min), an agent goal or tool call fails with an error whose traceback names a module that imports the repaired file (transitively, one level of imports). Threshold: ANY such failure — not a rate — because the failure is deterministic-attributable to the changed file.

signal_gate.budget: bounded per incident (1) + per day (mirrors repair_breaker daily cap)

watch_loop.runs_in: backend (server-side daemon in main.py lifespan), not just the CLI
watch_loop.decision: failure_class -> budget -> verify (2026 Self-Healing Orchestrators pattern)
watch_loop.ask_human_on: confidence_floor_not_met (never trusts the agent's own confidence; uses deterministic ranker)

approval_model.unattended_allowed: application-code repairs under the scope_ceiling + signal-gated rollback
human_approval_required: rollback broader than the evidence-justified diff
any repair that exceeds the daily/per-incident budget
